subject: Hosted commit uplift — onboarding plan and rateband mapping
messages:

Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted commit uplift — onboarding plan and rateband mapping

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for the conversation earlier — really excited to see PixelShift scale the new recommendations engine. Per our call you indicated you'd like to move from your current 1.2M token/month hosted commit to a 3.5M tier starting in November to support the A/B rollout.

Attached is a short proposal that outlines:
- committed tokens and monthly cadence
- planned ramp schedule (Nov-Jan) and burst pocket details
- proposed ratebands and soft-throttle thresholds

High-level asks: can you confirm the target start month (we have Nov 1 tentative), whether you want a 12- or 24-month term, and whether PixelShift requires a formal PO before DocuSign?

Next steps from our side: Marissa will finalize commercial language and Karthik will validate the ops handoff / soft-throttle mapping so there are no surprises during ramp.

Thanks,

Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0127

Irene,

Thanks — reviewed the doc and this looks roughly right. A few clarifications from our finance and platform teams:

1) Term: leaning toward 12-month with a 3-month ramp clause, but open to 24-month if there's a better price band.
2) PO: our procurement prefers a PO for amendments; our billing team will request an invoice once the DocuSign is processed.
3) Rate limits: the engineering team is worried about the soft-throttle behavior at the 15k RPS equivalent — can you confirm what exact behavior PixelShift will see if we push past the burst pocket? (latency vs partial accept vs queued)

Can Marissa or Karthik respond on the commercial and ops mapping and we can lock dates.

Best,
Elena
Head of Platform
PixelShift

Elena — quick commercial reply:

- Pricing: 3.5M token/month commit at the standard hosted uplift band (we can offer a 6% discount for a 24-month term).
- Ramp: we agree to a 3-month ramp with linear step-ups: 40% of commit in month 1, 75% in month 2, 100% in month 3.
- PO/Docs: If you need a PO for internal processing that’s fine — we can do DocuSign first and send an invoice once the PO is in place; legal prefers signed amendment then PO for SSO.

Irene — I attached the redlined amendment (same file name) and included a short clause for a one-time prorated charge if they go live mid-month. Elena — please confirm term and we’ll route for signature.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

marissa@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Cruz <elena@pixelshift.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 02 Oct 2026 15:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted commit uplift — onboarding plan and rateband mapping

Elena — ops/infra reply on the soft-throttle behavior and what to expect during burst exhaustion: 

- Normal behavior: requests are served with target p99 latency SLAs up to the committed token rate.
- Burst pocket: short-duration (up to configured burst tokens per minute) will be served at the same latency profile.
- Soft-throttle: once both burst and queued allowance are exhausted we do graceful degradation:
  * New requests receive HTTP 429 when we advise progressive backoff — we do not drop in-flight tokens mid-response.
  * For higher-priority routes you can opt-in to a prioritized lane (reserve X% of capacity) to avoid 429s for those calls.
  * In extreme sustained overload we fall back to a lower-cost model variant (auto-fallback) — that will increase latency and may alter token usage characteristics; we provide a changelog and warning events before any automatic fallback.

Operational ask: can PixelShift provide a list of critical endpoints you want prioritized during ramp (recommend top-5) and an expected traffic curve for Nov/Dec so we can pre-warm caches and pin model variants?

Irene/Marissa: I’ll prepare an ops runbook for the verified ramp (include soft-throttle thresholds, monitoring dashboards, and rollback play).

Karthik Iyer
Director, Inference Operations
